method: Retained 1x inputs; serial fresh processes; rotating three-backend order; separate prewarmed host/backend caches; warm filesystem caches; default Node heap; fixed affinity; production hosts; no concurrent heavy work. Historical TypeScript uses its frozen checkout with diagnostic-only benchmark additions. Caches were prewarmed by excluded setup and diagnostic runs. All three benchmark supervisors record and require worker exit zero. Production TypeScript is unchanged; only diagnostics and request sequences are patched. Earlier timing/parity probes are excluded.
scope: Source-text search after the initial unfiltered page; translation search is covered by differential tests, not timed here. Original TypeScript is the frozen complete engine, not the superseded hybrid.
completion: All 18 accepted runs reported done and exited with worker code 0 and no signal. All warm opens reused their joined view. No concurrent heavy work.
parity: All complete responses have identical canonical JSON hashes across all 18 runs for each of the 40 measured page operations. Canonicalization sorts object keys and preserves arrays and values; raw hashes are also retained.
excluded: native-search setup/preliminary timings and native-search-parity diagnostic runs are excluded. An unmeasured historical Workbench setup crashed inside Node's zstd worker and its unchanged retry passed. The final series reruns all three backends with canonical hashes and strict worker-exit diagnostics, including the frozen TypeScript control.
rejectedExperiment: Sorting count inputs into physical row order increased localization totals from about 27 to 33 ms in a private single-run stage probe; removed before the final candidate. No production changes follow 75a12e4f.
limitations: Three-run medians on one retained generated 1x dataset and warm filesystem caches, not universal budgets. Native opening now eagerly loads the existing folded arena, moving preparation out of the first typed search. Report opening and refresh costs separately. Peak RSS is sampled process-tree memory and includes overlapping reader generations; it is not a retained-cache size or guaranteed peak.
